Predict biomass over mapped canopy

Source: R/kb_predict_biomass_canopy.R
kb_predict_biomass_canopy.Rd

Predict the biomass over each row's mapped canopy from a cover calibration fit: wet, dry, carbon, or nitrogen (kg), optionally pooled by grouping columns.

Usage

kb_predict_biomass_canopy(
  fit,
  new_data,
  wetdry = NULL,
  carbon = NULL,
  nitrogen = NULL,
  ...,
  measure = c("wet", "dry", "carbon", "nitrogen"),
  pool_by = NULL,
  new_levels = c("sample", "average"),
  representative_site = NULL,
  conf_level = 0.95,
  estimate = stats::median,
  sig_fig = 3
)

Arguments

fit

A kb_fit_cover_calibration object.

new_data

A data frame of canopy maps, one row per map (see kb_check_data_survey_canopy() for the columns). Other columns are kept and can be named in pool_by. year may be numeric or character: 2022 and "2022" match the same fitted year.

wetdry

A kb_fit_wetdry object, required for dry, carbon, and nitrogen biomass, or NULL. All fits must be of the same species and have the same number of draws.

carbon

A kb_fit_carbon object, required for carbon biomass, or NULL.

nitrogen

A kb_fit_nitrogen object, required for nitrogen biomass, or NULL.

...

These dots are for future extensions and must be empty.

measure

A string, one of "wet", "dry", "carbon", or "nitrogen", giving the type of biomass to predict.

pool_by

A character vector naming character or factor columns to group the rows by, such as c("site", "year"), character(0) to pool all rows, or NULL (the default) for one row per input row. On each draw, the biomass of a group is the sum of its rows' biomass (kg). For another summary, such as an unweighted mean of rows, summarise the draws column, for example with posterior::rvar_mean().

new_levels

A string giving how uncertainty is shown for a site or year not in the fit. Sites and years in the fit always use their own estimates. One of:

  • "sample" (the default): a new effect for each new site or year, drawn from the estimated variation among sites or among years (the random-effect standard deviation). The point estimate is equivalent, but the interval is wider since it also includes that variation. Use it to get realistic uncertainty about a particular site or year that the model has no information on. The interval varies slightly between calls; use set.seed() to reproduce it.

  • "average": the typical site or year. The site and year effects are set to 0, their mean, so the interval does not include among-site or among-year variation. Use it to describe an average site or year.

representative_site

A character vector of sites in the fit whose effects a new site adopts (averaged when several are named), or NULL (the default) to follow new_levels.

conf_level

A number greater than 0 and less than 1 giving the compatibility-interval level.

estimate

A function that reduces a numeric vector of posterior draws to a single estimate, such as median or mean.

sig_fig

A whole number of significant figures for summary output.

Value

A kb_predictions object: the rows of new_data, or one row per pool_by group, with cover_support (when the rows have a site and year), the draws of the total (biomass_kg, dry_biomass_kg, carbon_biomass_kg, or nitrogen_biomass_kg), and estimate, lower, and upper.

Details

A row's total is the calibration at full cover times its tide-corrected canopy area, capped at classified_area_m2 (see Methods). A warning is given if a row is past the tide limit on more than 5% of draws, or if a pooled group has more than one map of a site-year, which counts its bed more than once.

See also

kb_predict_cover_calibration() for biomass per m² of a plot.

Other prediction functions: autoplot.kb_predictions(), kb_new_data(), kb_plot_predictions(), kb_predict_biomass_in_situ(), kb_predict_carbon(), kb_predict_cover_calibration(), kb_predict_mean_weight(), kb_predict_nitrogen(), kb_predict_size(), kb_predict_weight(), kb_predict_wetdry(), predict.kb_fit_carbon(), predict.kb_fit_cover_calibration(), predict.kb_fit_nitrogen(), predict.kb_fit_size(), predict.kb_fit_weight(), predict.kb_fit_wetdry()

Examples

fit <- fit_cover_calibration_sim_nereo

# One total per row
set.seed(1)
kb_predict_biomass_canopy(fit, data_survey_canopy_sim_nereo)
#> <kb_predictions> response: biomass_kg | by: site, year
#> # A tibble: 49 × 11
#>    site      year  canopy_area_m2 canopy_tide_height_m classified_area_m2 region
#>    <fct>     <fct>          <dbl>                <dbl>              <dbl> <fct> 
#>  1 otter_co… 2020            6817                 1.2               18504 north 
#>  2 gull_rock 2020           53242                 0.15             142539 north 
#>  3 cedar_bay 2020            5893                 1.05              11737 north 
#>  4 heron_re… 2020           24787                 0.6               51227 north 
#>  5 urchin_s… 2020           20431                 0.75              55633 south 
#>  6 sculpin_… 2020           16455                 1                 45632 south 
#>  7 eagle_sp… 2020           38273                 1.3               76960 south 
#>  8 tidepool… 2020           20110                 0.2               41234 south 
#>  9 otter_co… 2021            4819                 1.6                9556 north 
#> 10 gull_rock 2021           38877                 0.2               83128 north 
#> # ℹ 39 more rows
#> # ℹ 5 more variables: cover_support <chr>, biomass_kg <rvar[1d]>,
#> #   estimate <dbl>, lower <dbl>, upper <dbl>

# Wet totals by region and year
set.seed(1)
kb_predict_biomass_canopy(
  fit,
  data_survey_canopy_sim_nereo,
  pool_by = c("region", "year")
)
#> <kb_predictions> response: biomass_kg | by: region, year
#> # A tibble: 12 × 6
#>    region year         biomass_kg estimate  lower   upper
#>    <fct>  <fct>        <rvar[1d]>    <dbl>  <dbl>   <dbl>
#>  1 north  2020    989350 ± 144459   980000 735000 1310000
#>  2 north  2021    598562 ± 92683    594000 426000  781000
#>  3 north  2022    396554 ± 68212    391000 278000  543000
#>  4 north  2023    306940 ± 46859    304000 224000  406000
#>  5 north  2024    220094 ± 40111    221000 140000  298000
#>  6 north  2025    477421 ± 70150    469000 355000  639000
#>  7 south  2020   1110012 ± 141970  1090000 867000 1420000
#>  8 south  2021    549527 ± 75487    548000 410000  700000
#>  9 south  2022    566128 ± 75479    560000 433000  732000
#> 10 south  2023    369234 ± 49059    366000 281000  475000
#> 11 south  2024    262608 ± 41242    263000 176000  343000
#> 12 south  2025    853358 ± 121528   841000 650000 1120000

# Carbon stock by year
set.seed(1)
kb_predict_biomass_canopy(
  fit,
  data_survey_canopy_sim_nereo,
  fit_wetdry_sim_nereo,
  fit_carbon_sim_nereo,
  measure = "carbon",
  pool_by = "year"
)
#> <kb_predictions> response: carbon_biomass_kg | by: year
#> # A tibble: 6 × 5
#>   year  carbon_biomass_kg estimate lower upper
#>   <fct>        <rvar[1d]>    <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
